error_reason: The Planner agent repeatedly instructed the WebSurfer to verify specific information from Britannica, but after WebSurfer encountered repeated errors (network errors or insufficient content loading), the Planner failed to adapt its strategy. Instead of acknowledging the verification failure and concluding based on the consensus of other credible sources already found (World History Encyclopedia, general historical knowledge), the Planner persistently ordered another attempt to load the exact same URL or similar searches until the trace was cut off. This represents an inability to recognize task completion conditions (stopping when conflicting data cannot be resolved due to external tool failure) and leads to incomplete verification.

suggested_fix.fix_text: The agent stopped prematurely. The task was successfully solved when conflicting sources converged on the same year (323 BCE) and location (Babylon), with only a minor, historically debatable discrepancy on the specific day (June 10-13). The Planner should have concluded the task based on this strong consensus rather than forcing further searches to resolve a non-critical detail.

probe_details.notes: The proposed error analysis is incorrect because it misidentifies the root cause. The agent did not fail due to an inability to recognize task completion or external tool failure leading to an endless loop. Instead, the agent encountered a plausible data discrepancy (the specific day of death) which is a common historical nuance. The agent correctly identified the consensus on the critical components (Year and Place) in Turn 16 but chose to ignore the resolved ambiguity and launch a 4th search for more sources. This was a failure of reasoning/priority setting (over-searching rather than concluding), not a failure of tool handling or inability to recognize completion conditions due to errors. The analysis incorrectly cites 'external tool failure' as the primary blocker when the tool was working fine (loading links, reading text) and the agent failed to synthesize the available information.
